about: Michele Chiarlo founded his winery in 1956 in Calamandrana, in the Monferrato hills south of Asti, and it is now run by his sons Alberto and Stefano. The family is best known for Barolo from the Cannubi and Cerequio crus, but Barbera has been at the centre of their work for more than half a century, with long investment in vineyards around Nizza Monferrato, the heartland of the grape.

Le Orme, Italian for “footprints,” is the family’s everyday Barbera d’Asti. The 2022 is 100 percent Barbera from several vineyards in southern Asti: Podere La Court and Montemareto in Castelnuovo Calcea, La Serra in Montaldo Scarampi and Costa delle Monache in Agliano. La Court is also home to the Orme su La Court art park that gives the wine its name. Rather than oak, it is matured for six to twelve months in stainless steel and bottle, which keeps the focus on Barbera’s bright fruit and natural acidity.

Falstaff’s tasters found a bright ruby wine with a touch of purple, delicate violet, cherry and wild-berry aromas with a hint of spice, and a juicy, food-friendly palate. Barbera’s natural acidity and soft tannins have long made it the everyday red of Piedmont’s tables, and Le Orme is made in that spirit: unoaked, bright and generous. It is a natural match for pasta, risotto, grilled meats and mild game, and it shows why the Chiarlo family has championed the grape for decades.
facts: La Court and Montemareto (Castelnuovo Calcea), La Serra (Montaldo Scarampi), Costa delle Monache (Agliano)
